newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet says will pay 893 mln DM for Serbian deal.
newsitem.headline: Stet says will pay 893 mln DM for Serbian deal.

text.p: Italian telecommunications company Stet will pay 893 million German marks for its 29 percent stake in Serbia Telekom, the group said in a statement on Monday.
It said 702 million marks would be handed over when the deal was fully finalised and a further 191 million by January 1998.
Under the terms of the agreement announced in Belgrade earlier on Monday, Greece's OTE will take a 20 percent stake in Serbia Telekom.
Stet said the Greek group would pay 675 million marks for the holding -- 543 million at the closing and 132 million marks by January 1998.
The deal involved Stet providing technical assistance to the Serbian firm, "with a return calculated in percentage terms on the turnover of the Serbian operator," Stet said.
"In addition, Stet/Telecom Italia will have a significant role in the running of the company," the statement added.
Stet and operating company Telecom Italia are due to merge next month ahead of the privatisation of the group, which is slated for later this year.

"The prospects for growth in the Serbian telecommunications market...are particularly favourable, taking into account that telecommunication services and economic performance have been artificially depressed for five years by the recent Balkan war," Stet said.
It said Telecom Serbia had around two million clients representing a 20 percent penetration into the local market.

The firm had turnover of around 600 billion lire in 1996 with a gross operating profit of around 375 billion. "The forecasts for development in 1997 see strong growth with turnover which could exceed 900 billion (lire)," Stet said.
It added that the number of clients were expected to double over the next 10 years, with turnover by the end of that period hitting some two trillion lire.
Investments during that time will total some 5.2 billion German marks. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
